name: Marathon Digital Holdings

profile.address: Mitchell Bend Highway, Hood County, Texas, 76048
profile.reading: This is a large-scale Bitcoin mining facility on the Mitchell Bend Highway site in Hood County (Granbury), Texas, run "behind the meter" at the Wolf Hollow natural gas generating station rather than as a conventional leased-power data center. Wolf Hollow itself dates to 2003 (788 megawatts) with a second phase, Wolf Hollow II, added in 2017 (1,115 megawatts); Compute North, an earlier cryptocurrency-mining infrastructure company, broke ground on a roughly 300-megawatt mining facility at the site in 2022 to consume power directly from the plant. Compute North filed for bankruptcy in 2022, and MARA Holdings (formerly Marathon Digital Holdings) acquired the Hood County facility in January 2024, with MARA describing full operations beginning that April. The company reports creating about 19 jobs at the site since acquisition and employing roughly 21 people locally, alongside more than $100,000 in annual community giving to Granbury ISD, United Way, and the local Chamber of Commerce. The facility runs thousands of specialized mining computers around the clock, and its constant cooling-fan noise became the subject of sustained community conflict: in October 2024, Earthjustice filed a nuisance lawsuit in Hood County state court on behalf of Citizens Concerned About Wolf Hollow, identifying more than two dozen nearby residents reporting hearing loss, migraines, tinnitus, and vertigo attributed to continuous mining noise, and separate reporting (including a Time magazine investigation) documented the broader community health fallout. In response, MARA states it has converted about 40 percent of the site to immersion cooling -- a quieter method that submerges hardware in liquid rather than relying on banks of air-cooled fans -- and completed sound-wall construction by November 2024, reporting resulting sound levels of roughly 43-63 decibels versus an 85-decibel legal limit. The facility also participates in ERCOT demand-response programs, curtailing its own power draw within minutes during grid stress or price spikes to free capacity for the broader Texas grid. As a proof-of-work mining site rather than a commercial colocation facility, no square-footage, IT-load, or uptime-certification figures in the traditional data-center sense are published; the facility's relevant public specifications are its interconnected power draw and its noise and demand-response record.

reading:
MARA Holdings, headquartered in Hallandale Beach, Florida and trading on Nasdaq as MARA under SEC filer number 0001507605, is one of the largest publicly traded bitcoin miners in the world, led by chief executive Fred Thiel. Its corporate history is unusual: it was incorporated in 2010 as Marathon Patent Group, a patent holding and litigation business operating through its Uniloc subsidiary, renamed itself Marathon Digital Holdings on March 1, 2021 as it moved into cryptocurrency, and became MARA Holdings on August 29, 2024. It reported holding 50,639 bitcoin as of August 2025. It belongs in this registry as a power first computing operator rather than a colocation landlord, since it mines for its own account at sites chosen for cheap electricity.

The facility recorded here is on Mitchell Bend Highway in Hood County, Texas, near Granbury, and it runs behind the meter at the Wolf Hollow natural gas generating complex, whose first unit dates to 2003 at 788 megawatts and whose second, Wolf Hollow II, was added in 2017 at 1,115 megawatts. Those are plant generation ratings and have nothing to do with the mine's own load. The mining site was built in 2022 by Compute North, which broke ground on a project scoped at roughly 300 megawatts. Compute North filed for bankruptcy later that year and MARA acquired the Hood County site in January 2024. The 300 megawatt figure is the original project scope and not a confirmed operating figure for MARA, which publishes no IT load for Granbury.

The community record here is far more detailed than anything the operator publishes, and it is the reason this site is well known. The Texas Tribune reported the mine running close to 60,000 computers roughly half a mile from homes. Residents sued in 2024 in a nuisance case brought with Earthjustice, alleging health effects from continuous noise. A third party study funded by the county in October 2024 measured about 60 decibels near the facility and 35 to 53 decibels in neighborhoods within a mile, against resident readings just below the 85 decibel level used as the state threshold. MARA built a sound wall roughly 2,000 feet long and 24 feet tall and replaced about two thirds of its cooling fans with immersion cooling. County Commissioner Nannette Samuelson said she could hear the site from six miles away, and county commissioners asked the legislature without success for stricter state noise rules. About 600 residents in a two square mile area, including roughly 250 registered voters, then petitioned to incorporate a town called Mitchell Bend in order to gain zoning and noise authority. County Judge Ron Massingill rejected the first petition in August 2025 and accepted a revised one. MARA sued Hood County and its officials to stop the vote, a federal judge denied its request for a temporary restraining order, and on November 4, 2025 the measure failed with 52 of 138 votes cast in favor. The Earthjustice noise case continues, and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality has separately handled a contested air permit for another gas plant near the site.
